LESSON: WRITING 10.4.1 CREATIVE WRITING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 10
Topic 10.4: Writing 10.4.1 Creative Writing

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 10.4.1 Creative Writing. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why should you organise your thoughts in clear sentences and paragraphs?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe the parts of a descriptive composition for self-expression
2. create a descriptive composition of about 80- 100 words on various topics for effective communication

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 10.4.1 CREATIVE WRITING
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 10.4.1 Creative Writing helps you succeed in ENGLISH LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 10.4.1 CREATIVE WRITING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Describe the parts of a descriptive composition for self-expression

What this means
In this part you learn to describe the parts of a descriptive composition for self-expression. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe the parts of a descriptive composition for self-expression.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 10.4.1 Creative Writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe the parts of a descriptive composition for self-expression. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Create a descriptive composition of about 80- 100 words on various topics for effective communication

What this means
In this part you learn to create a descriptive composition of about 80- 100 words on various topics for effective communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: create a descriptive composition of about 80- 100 words on various topics for effective communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 10.4.1 Creative Writing to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can create a descriptive composition of about 80- 100 words on various topics for effective communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 10.4.1 Creative Writing is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 10.4.1 Creative Writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: describe the parts of a descriptive composition for self-expression)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 10.4.1 Creative Writing to a partner. (skill: create a descriptive composition of about 80- 100 words on various topics for effective communication)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 10.4.1 Creative Writing to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: describe the parts of a descriptive composition for self-expression.
3. Practise this skill: create a descriptive composition of about 80- 100 words on various topics for effective communication.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 10.4.1 Creative Writing from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 10.4.1 Creative Writing: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Writing 10.4.1 Creative Writing?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should you organise your thoughts in clear sentences and paragraphs?
2. How can you tell others about yourself?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 10.4.1 Creative Writing means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: describe the parts of a descriptive composition for self-expression.
5. Be able to: create a descriptive composition of about 80- 100 words on various topics for effective communication.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
